title: What If the Ozone Layer Vanished?

scenes.text: What if the ozone layer vanished? The sunlight itself becomes the danger.
The ozone layer sits about fifteen miles up. It absorbs the sun's most harmful UV rays, like a natural sunscreen.
NASA simulated a world where it kept eroding. By twenty forty, summer UV in cities like Washington hit fifteen. Ten is already very high.
By twenty sixty-five, two thirds of the layer was gone and ground-level UV had doubled. More skin cancer, more cataracts, weaker immune systems.
In a NASA lab, a basil plant under intense UV browned within an hour and died within a day.
The ocean would suffer too. UV harms phytoplankton, the base of the sea's food web.

description:
What if the ozone layer vanished?
UV rays would damage skin, eyes, plants and the plankton that feed the oceans.
